main_body: A square hay bale filling the tile, drawn as one flat golden-yellow panel split by a vertical dark brown strap and a horizontal seam, with a darker olive-brown border around it.
top_band: none. A single central column runs from a dark border (rows 2-3) straight into the same yellow straw tone with no lighter horizontal band and no step. The straw is one continuous face from row 3 to row 13.
evidence: The bale is a flat square seen face-on. The border is only a thin 1-2px frame. The straw tone runs uninterrupted from the top rim to the bottom rim, with a vertical strap and a horizontal seam drawn on it as surface decoration. There is no distinct lighter top surface, no front-edge line and no eave shadow under a top. This matches the guide's front elevation / top-down slab failure, not a 3/4 box.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark olive-brown, which leans toward the straw, so it reads as tinted rather than black. The straw has two or three tones with scattered dark dots, which gives some texture. The straw is only about 3 steps (light, mid, dark), against 5-6 in the references. The strap is flat brown. Each tile carries only a handful of colours, well under the reference density of the stall and well. Next to the stall and well the piece looks thin and flat.
